purpose: Fix the bar the FINAL frozen policy must clear before the three sealed circuits may be opened.

final_circuit_protocol.seed_band: reserved final-circuit band, disjoint from train/validation/test

timing_disclosure.statement: This supersedes the readiness_thresholds recorded in pre_registration.json, whose hash was d4b90bdf... That file remains unedited: a pre-registration is not rewritten after the fact, it is superseded in the open.
what_already_existed_when_this_was_writt: the matched VALIDATION selection benchmark over the five candidate checkpoints, and therefore the identity of FINAL_PPO_PARENT (ppo_729088)
what_did_not_yet_exist: the difficulty-ladder evaluation, at any rung, for any policy
the final hard-case continuation run and its checkpoints
any evaluation whatsoever of the policy this gate will judge
any contact with the three sealed circuits
timing_disclosure.why_that_is_the_relevant_property: This gate judges the FINAL frozen policy on ladder plus matched evidence. None of that evidence exists yet, and the policy itself has not been trained yet, so the bar is genuinely fixed ahead of what it measures. Knowing which parent was selected cannot tune a bar applied to a policy that does not exist.

correction.what: An earlier copy of this file recorded thresholds hash 783f6775..., computed while primary_difficulty was G2.
correction.why_it_was_wrong: G2 contradicted the module's own stated rationale ('the one regime every candidate actually trained in') and its tests, and was left by a verification agent that died mid-edit on a session limit. The matched benchmark ran at G1, and matched_difficulty is a NON-OVERRIDABLE evidence criterion, so a G2 bar would have permanently blocked readiness on a stray edit rather than on any property of the policy.
correction.when: before any ladder evaluation existed, so no evidence was reread against a moved bar

revision.changed: required_difficulty G6 -> primary_difficulty G1 plus a ladder requirement
revision.reason: The original G6 bar was unmeetable by construction and therefore uninformative: every candidate trained exclusively at G1 because promotion requires >=0.99 success with zero safety events, which no evaluation ever achieved. But a plain G1 bar would certify competence earned entirely on near-straight, near-level, near-aligned geometry. The revision keeps G1 as the primary matched difficulty and adds a non-overridable EVIDENCE requirement that a mid-ladder rung (G3 or above, the first rung with real vertical structure at 1.20 m against G1's 0.20 m) was actually run with a real sample, plus a competence requirement that the policy does not collapse there. A policy cannot pass by only ever being tested on the easy rung.
revision.decided_before: any ladder evaluation had been run, for any policy

non_overridable: every evidence criterion, including ladder coverage and the matched dataset split
